To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the oxygen and carbon isotopic records of a stalagmites from Buddha Cave in central China have recorded climate changes over the last 1.3 kyr, including those corresponding to the Little Ice Age and Medieval Warm Period, and also reveal cycles of 33 22 11 9.6 and 7. 2 years.

the oxygen and carbon isotope records of stalagmite SF-1 from central China reveal climate changes over the last 1300 years, and these records contain cycles that may be linked to solar and lunar variations.
the oxygen and carbon isotopic compositions in a 1270-year-old stalagmite from central China record the Medieval Warm Period, Little Ice Age and the 20th-century global warming.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reconstruction of past climatic variability in central China.
the reconstruction of climate variability in central China and the relationship between climate variability and solar forcing over the last millennium.
the reconstruction of climate change in central China over a period of 1270 years, based on a stalagmite record from Buddha Cave (Hunan Province).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
climate variability in central China during the past 1270 years is dominated by solar forcing and the ENSO cycle.
the SF-1 stalagmite records reveal a series of climate cycles in the last 1275 years.

the stable isotope composition of speleothems is a reliable proxy for paleoclimatic reconstructions in central China and that the 22, 33, 9.61, 11, or 7.2 year periodicities are probably solar or solar-related forcing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the climate variability in central China has been modulated by the external forcing and internal dynamics.

the climate variability over central China for the past 1270 years has been characterized by a 33-year periodicity and a 7.2- to 9.6-year periodicity, with a strong 22- to 11-year periodicity superimposed on the former.
the stable isotope variations in stalagmites from central China can be used to reconstruct climate changes over the past 1270 years with a time resolution as high as 1–2 years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high-resolution stalagmites provide an important tool for understanding climate change and climate forcing in China and other parts of the world.
the climate of central China over the past 1270 years was highly variable, with the 11-year solar cycle playing a major role.
the climate variability over the last 1300 years in central China has been dominated by the summer monsoon.
